objectives: Say what a good friend does.
Show a good friend you care in everyday ways.
Share and take turns with a friend.
Tell the truth to a friend and say sorry when you are wrong.
Stay friendly when you and a friend disagree.

sections.body:
A good friend is a person you can be yourself around. That is the whole secret.

With a good friend, you do not have to pretend. If you are sad, you can be sad. If you are silly, you can be silly. If you are scared, you can say so. A good friend does not laugh at the parts of you that are not perfect.

A good friend **listens**. They look at you while you talk. They remember the small things you said. They do not try to win the conversation.

A good friend **shares**. They give you their things and let you give yours. They share their time as well as their toys.

A good friend **tells the truth**. Not a mean truth. A kind truth. If you have a hole in your shoe, a good friend tells you and helps you fix it.

A good friend **helps**. When you fall over, they help you up. When you cannot find something, they look with you.

And a good friend **comes back**. Friends quarrel. That is normal. What matters is that a good friend walks back to you afterwards.

You do not have to have many friends. One good friend is worth more than ten people who ignore you. And friendship grows quietly, one small day at a time.
examples: You can be yourself with a good friend.
She listens when I am sad.
A good friend tells you the truth kindly.
sections.heading: What a good friend is

sections.body:
Friendship is built out of small things. You do not need a big plan. You need small good habits.

**Remember what they told you.** If your friend said their grandma was ill, ask about her next day. That small question says *I was listening*.

**Invite them in.** Sometimes you are playing happily and a new child stands nearby looking lonely. Saying *come and play with us* costs nothing and means a lot.

**Include them at the table.** In Vietnam, meals are often the best part of the day. Saving a place for a friend is a real gift.

**Help without being asked.** If their pencil falls, pick it up. If they cannot reach something, fetch it.

**Say something nice.** *You are good at that* is a simple sentence that makes somebody's day.

**Make time.** A good friend does not only show up when there is something fun. A good friend also comes when your friend is ill or sad.

Try one of these this week. Just one. Then see how it feels.
examples: You are really good at drawing.
sections.heading: How you show a friend you care

sections.body:
These are the words grown-ups use for friendship. Learn them and you can talk about your friends.

A **friend** is a person you like and who likes you back. Friends like to spend time together.

**Sharing** means letting somebody use your things, and letting them do things with you too.

**Taking turns** means one goes first and then the other one goes. Turns are how two people use one thing fairly.

**Listening** means giving your attention to somebody who is talking. Your eyes and your body show that you are listening.

**Trust** is when you believe somebody will be kind and honest with you. Trust is built slowly and lost quickly.

**Honesty** means telling the truth, even when it is hard. Honest friends tell you kindly.

A **quarrel** is when two friends get angry with each other. A quarrel is normal. It is not the end of a friendship.

**Making up** means you come back to each other after a quarrel. Both people have to move a little.
examples: I trust my friend to keep a secret.
We took turns on the slide.
We made up after our quarrel.

terms.example: We had a quarrel and made up the same afternoon.
terms.gloss: When two friends get angry with each other. Every friendship has these.

sections.body:
Almost every friendship has a quarrel. What matters is what you do next.

First, wait a little. If you are still hot, do not go and talk yet. Let the heat go down.

Then, think about your part. Not only their part. What did you do? Every quarrel has two sides.

Next, go and find them. Go first if you have to. Say sorry for your part, without adding *but*.

Then, listen to their part. Do not interrupt to explain. Let them finish.

After that, fix the thing if you can. Return the toy. Pay back the lost marble. Say what you will do next time.

Finally, make a plan to meet again. *Let's play after school tomorrow.* A friendship needs a next time to be safe.

If your friend is not ready yet, give them a day. Send a message. Say *I am sorry and I still want to be your friend.* Then wait. Most friendships come back on their own.
examples: Sorry I said that. It was unkind.
I still want to be your friend.
sections.heading: How to make up after a quarrel
steps: Think about your part in the quarrel.
Make a plan to meet again.

sections.body:
Sometimes a friendship is difficult, and that is not your fault.

Some children tease. Some children take things. Some children say no to everything. You cannot change how somebody behaves, and it is not your job to fix it.

What you can do is talk to a grown-up you trust. A teacher, a parent, a family member. Tell them what happened, in order: what you saw, how you felt, and what you want to happen next.

If somebody hurts you, that is never your fault, whatever you did before. Tell an adult straight away. You will not get in trouble for telling the truth.

If you feel lonely most days, tell somebody. Loneliness is a real feeling and grown-ups can help with it.

And if a friendship keeps hurting, it is okay to step back and find kinder people. Walking away from unkindness is not rudeness. It is wisdom.
examples: He keeps taking my things and I feel sad about it.
Can we talk about what happened?
I do not want to play with him today.
sections.heading: When a friendship is hard

sections.body:
Being a good friend is easy on a happy day. The real test comes when something goes wrong.

Your friend is playing with somebody else. Your friend says no to your invitation. Your friend forgets your birthday. Your friend does not agree with you.

A good friend does not punish you for these things. They do not bring them up every week. They shrug, and they keep being there.

Try this: **say how you feel once, calmly, and then let it go.** *I felt left out yesterday. I am fine now.* That is honest and kind. It gives your friend a chance to fix it without pressure.

Sometimes your friend will hurt you on purpose. Then you do not have to keep being kind to that. You can say *I do not like it when you say that* and walk away. Being kind is not the same as being a pushover.

And sometimes you are the one who was unkind. Owning it quickly makes you a better friend than almost anyone. *I was wrong. I am sorry.*

Friendship is not a thing you have. It is a thing you do, again and again, on ordinary days.
examples: I felt left out yesterday. I am fine now.
I do not like it when you say that.
I was wrong. I am sorry.
sections.heading: Being a good friend when it is hard

item.summary: A good friend listens, shares, tells the truth, and stays close. After reading this you can pick a good friend, be a good friend yourself, and fix a friendship after a quarrel.
